title: Symphony batcher: continuous workload-tuning, KV-cache heuristics and safe apply curator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a continuous recommendation engine ("Symphony batcher") that synthesizes workload profiles, KV prefix/caching heuristics, and time-windowed batching parameters to produce safe, incremental config updates. The engine must surface explainable candidate changes, validate them via shadow simulation, and apply them through a staged, rollback-capable pipeline with observability hooks for cost/latency/regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: Engine can ingest per-route traffic traces and output per-route recommended batch_size, max_latency_ms, kv_prefix_cache_window and an explainability score
Shadow simulator runs recommended configs against historical traces with quantifiable cost/latency deltas and failure-mode detection
Canary rollout automation applies config to 1%/10%/100% with automatic rollback on latency or error regression thresholds
UI/Console surface shows top 5 drivers for a given recommendation (e.g., dominant sequence length distribution, high microburst metric, cold KV miss rate)
Telemetry exports: per-recommendation diff, apply/rollback events, and SLO breach correlation tags
implementation_notes: Profile schema: use existing workload-signature proto (route, model_version, seq_len_histogram, interarrival_cdf, kv_miss_rate, cpu_gpu_usage) with a new 'temporal_bucket' field
Heuristics: combine three signals (cost-slope at 95th latency, kv-miss-induced token penalty, and microburstiness score) with weighted scoring; weights are feature-flagged and tunable
Simulator: deterministic replayer + small-scale inference emulator to stress KV and batching effects on latency distribution; keep compute bounded by sampling (10% of requests by route)
Safety: every recommendation gets a 'rollback guard' generated: metric thresholds and a dependency list (models/runtimes impacted)
Config model: record candidate as a JSON patch referencing route id + model variant; audits stored in bucket with checksum
rollout_plan: 1) Offline synthesis: run engine nightly on last 7 days of traces and produce candidate catalog
2) Shadow simulation: for top-k candidates run 3-day shadow replay; require no more than 2% P95 latency increase and >=3% token-cost reduction for proceed
3) Staged apply: Canary 1% traffic for 2 hours -> evaluate cost/latency/error; if healthy, 10% for 6 hours; if healthy, full apply rollout over 24 hours
4) Monitoring: dedicated dashboards for candidate_id that show latency percentiles, error rate, token cost, KV hit rate, and canary health
5) Post-apply audit: auto-generate PRD-like summary linking dash snapshots and simulation results
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: +10% relative P95 latency, +0.5% absolute error rate, or no cost improvement after 24h

Manual rollback procedure: call the curator service 'revert-to-prior' with candidate_id -> orchestrator replays prior config patch; ensure KV cache eviction windows are restored carefully to avoid thundering herd
Emergency path: escalate to on-call SRE and toggle global hold flag to prevent further automated applies
Post-rollback diagnostics: store traces from before/during/after rollback for root-cause analysis
